title: Install or recover the Chancery reader
summary: Install, inspect, or recover Chancery programs and their provider selector. Deployment runs the product-owned file and setup recipe.
use_when: Chancery programs should be installed, inspected, or recovered.
do_not_use_when: Another product must be deployed or its provider selector repaired.
The caller needs to alter or delete usage history.
outcome: The supplied programs and provider are selected together, or an explicit setup failure.
effects: Retain supplied programs and documentation in release archives and publish regular files at fixed runtime paths under installation locks. Public file selectors use runtime paths; provider directory selectors use the selected retained archive. Preserve other product selectors and separate product data.
authority: Chancery owns its program installation and provider selector. The operator supplies artifacts and authorizes selection.
success: Owned command and provider selectors follow the supplied release. Installation runs no signature audit, executable probe, or operational-readiness gate.
failure_and_recovery: Refuse foreign public selectors or stale expected-current selections. An instruction failure retains completed file and selector changes for explicit recovery. Recovery selects retained program files and leaves product data unchanged.
privacy: Install public local documentation without secrets. The separate private journal retains only command identity, thread, and observation time.
does_not_authorize: Changing another product release or provider selector.
Executing represented capabilities, clearing usage history, or editing installed immutable releases.
steps: Select the intended supplied binary and provider paths and the installation home.
Read the current selection and run install with any intended expected-current guard.
Register the installed command inventory separately and read installation metadata.
Recover a retained release when requested; keep diagnostics separate from installation.
checkpoints: Owned selectors select the supplied program and provider release.
The requested file placement and product setup have completed. Program selection does not establish application correctness or live readiness.
adaptation: Use absolute paths and an intentional alternate home when required.
stop_when: Required files cannot be copied, a selector is foreign, the expected selection changed, or a required setup operation fails.

consumers.statement: Current-user macOS operators may install, inspect or recover the Chancery reader.

preconditions.statement: Supplied program and provider paths, an intended installation home, and authority to change owned selectors. Installation does not require a validation receipt.

inputs.statement: Absolute binary and bundle paths, optional home and expected-current selection, or one retained release path for recovery.

outputs.statement: Recorded release metadata and selected public paths, or an installation error. Inspection reports metadata without checking artifact integrity.

data_semantics.statement: Program selection is installation state. It establishes neither database integrity nor dependency readiness nor domain success.

identity_and_units.statement: Opaque UUID release IDs name retained archives; executable files run at fixed actual paths beneath Chancery/install/runtime. Product releases, provider contract versions, and application state versions remain distinct. Installation does not compare component versions or artifact hashes.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: Inspection reads current selectors and recorded installation metadata. It does not audit retained content or probe a live dependency.

access.statement: The current-user macOS installer modifies only its owned installation and selectors and rejects foreign targets. Optional --home selects an explicit user home.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: Product and catalog locks serialize publication. Regular runtime files are replaced atomically at fixed actual paths; the complete tree is not one atomic update. Expected-current guards detect changed selection. An instruction failure retains completed file and selector changes for explicit recovery. Recovery reads retained metadata without integrity validation and preserves separate product state.

operational_limits.statement: Installation copies files and performs product-owned setup without running executable probes or native-signature audits. It runs no installer verify command, database integrity check, provider validation, or readiness probe. Explicit ordinary diagnostic commands keep their existing behavior.

Deploy accepts one bounded schema-two recipe request on stdin. The product command owns its setup; the shared executor uses process exit status only. Deployment runs no application execution probe, native-signature audit, maintenance hold, drain, or automatic rollback.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: The installer retains its archive layout and supported legacy metadata readers. Install and recovery publish regular runtime files at fixed actual paths and migrate owned older command selectors to that tree. Installer verify and verify-release commands are removed. Program recovery does not restore product data.

reliances.statement: This attended current-user operation uses local owned artifacts and creates no reliance on represented product runtime, network services, or Nucleus readiness.
